message.content: Roger presented for his initial intake session reporting significant distress related to anxiety and depression. He stated that he is not feeling the greatest and finds it difficult to focus, which makes other aspects of his life feel off. His standardized screening scores indicated low levels of anxiety and depression at 2 and 3 respectively, suggesting these are not currently severe. The primary source of current distress appears to be the lack of cognitive focus rather than mood severity. He is currently residing at the Turning Point shelter while collecting disability benefits for a traumatic brain injury. We discussed his history of substance use, but Roger noted he has no current desire to use substances because they cause too many problems. I utilized psychoeducation to validate his experience with post-concussive symptoms and explored coping strategies for managing daily stressors. Roger responded well to this approach by acknowledging the connection between his TBI and his difficulty concentrating. He expressed willingness to engage in future sessions to develop better focus techniques.
